caption: Performance of different tuning methods on GLUE for RoBERTa-base and RoBERTa-large. Here we also include two random baselines: (i) S_0-model, where all the designs are randomly selected for RoBERTa. (ii) S_3-model, where we randomly assign strategies to different RoBERTa layers while following the other design choices we learn from T5 models.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the GLUE performance of various fine-tuning methods applied to RoBERTa-base (blue bars) and RoBERTa-large (orange bars), with performance measured on the vertical axis ranging from approximately 85 to 90. The horizontal axis lists the fine-tuning methods: Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, and S₅-model. For each method, two bars are shown side-by-side, representing the performance of the base and large model variants. The legend in the upper left corner indicates that blue corresponds to RoBERTa-base and orange to RoBERTa-large. In general, the large model consistently outperforms the base model across all methods. The highest performance is achieved by the S₅-model with RoBERTa-large, reaching approximately 89.5, while the lowest is observed with the Prefix method on RoBERTa-base, around 85.2. The LoRA method shows a large performance gap between base (~86.5) and large (~89.2), while S₁-model shows nearly identical performance for both models (~85.5). The S₄-model and S₅-model both show significant improvements for the large model over the base, with S₅-model achieving the highest overall score. The bars are arranged in a grouped fashion for each fine-tuning method, and the chart does not include error bars or statistical annotations.
